full_source_report:
The study shows flexion contracture with posterior translation of the tibiafibula in respect to the distal femur, representing posterior dislocation.  
  
 In the medial compartment, there is macerated torn entire medial meniscus. There is diffuse low grade and high grade chondrosis (less than and more than 50% thickness cartilage loss) at weightbaring, non weightbaring medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau. Osteophytes are noted.  
  
 The lateral compartment, macerated torn entire lateral meniscus is note. There is diffuse low grade and high grade chondrosis (less than and more than 50% thickness cartilage loss) at weightbaring, non weightbaring lateral femoral condyle and lateral tibial plateau. There is no subchondral edema. Few subchondral bone cysts (about cm) are identified. Osteophytes are noted.  
  
 The patellofemoral joint, there is diffuse low grade and high grade chondrosis (less than and more than 50% thickness cartilage loss) along medial, lateral patellar facets, medial and lateral trochleas. There is no subchondral edema. Osteophytes are identified.  The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact  
  
 In the intercondylar notch, there is chronic complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. There is stretching with near complete tear and fibrotic scar at the posterior cruciate ligament.   
  
 There is chronic tear of the medial collateral ligament complexes. 
 There is chronic tear of the lateral collateral ligament complexes. 
  
 The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 Minimal amount of left knee effusion with synovitis and some fibrosis. The surrounding musculature is normal.  Flexion contracture with posterior translation of the tibiafibula in respect to the distal femur: left posterior knee dislocation. 
  Tricompartmental osteoarthritis of the left knee by evidence of chondrosis and osteophytes. 
  Macerated torn entire medial and lateral menisci. 
  Chronic complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.  
  Stretching with near complete tear and fibrotic scar at the posterior cruciate ligament.   
  Chronic tear of the medial and lateral collateral ligamentous complexes. 
  Minimal left knee effusion with synovitis and arthrofibrosis.
